title: FRust compile errors and how to fix them
summary: What each common FRust compile error means and how to fix it.
alternateQueries: Why does my FRust script not compile?
What does 'has no return value' mean?

blocks.text: A compile error names a line and column in your script. The cause is often on the line BEFORE the one named.

symptoms: unexpected STRING_LITERAL, expecting }  (or unexpected IDENT, expecting })
blocks.cause: A block statement (`if`, `else`, `while`, `for`, `match`) is followed by more code but its closing brace has no `;`. Or an `if`/`while` condition is a bare name before `{`, which is read as a struct value.
blocks.resolution: Write `};` after the block, and put every condition in parentheses: `if (ok) { ... };`.

blocks.cause: A macro such as format!(...) or println!(...) was used. FRust has no macros.
blocks.resolution: Return a plain string literal, and report numbers with station_log_i64 or station_log_f64.

symptoms: cannot call a method on an expression of unknown struct type
blocks.cause: A method was called on a value that has none, such as "x".to_string() or n.abs().
blocks.resolution: Values have no methods. Use plain functions from the API; only a struct with an `impl` block has methods.
Nest the if blocks, or write `if ((a == 1) & (b == 2)) { ... }`; use | for or.

symptoms: the operator '+' does not work on text
blocks.cause: Text was added, subtracted or otherwise combined with an operator. There is no string concatenation.
blocks.resolution: Report separate pieces with separate station_log calls.

blocks.cause: The last line of the function ends with `;` or is not an expression.
blocks.resolution: End the function with an expression and no `;`, for example the text to report.

symptoms: the condition of 'if' must be a true/false value or a number, not text
blocks.cause: A String was used as a condition.
blocks.resolution: Compare it first, or use a number or a true/false value.

symptoms: the two branches of this 'if' give different kinds of value
blocks.cause: One branch gives a number and the other text.
blocks.resolution: Make both branches give the same kind of value.

symptoms: the script has no `pub fn run() -> String`
blocks.cause: The entry function is missing or named differently.

symptoms: argument N of 'f' must be ..., or 'f' takes N argument(s)
blocks.cause: A call passes the wrong number or kind of arguments.
blocks.resolution: Check the function's declaration in the Station script API topic.

reviewedBy: Claude (from the FRust grammar and the compiler, not yet reviewed by a person)
